questions.question: Give an example of healthcare demand being income elastic.
questions.solution_html:
• Income elastic demand means demand changes with the changes in income -Example —
  • preference for private hospital care in Kerala - When income rises, people prefer private
  • hospitals instead of public ones -Health services are seen as a superior good -Shows positive
  • relation between income and healthcare demand

questions.question: Explain the poverty–malnutrition trap.
questions.solution_html:
• Poverty–malnutrition trap means a cycle linking low income and poor health -Poor people
  • cannot afford enough nutritious food - Leads to low productivity and poor health -Low
  • productivity reduces income again -The cycle of poverty and malnutrition continues across
  • generations.

questions.question: How does investment in public health promote inclusive and sustainable development?
questions.solution_html:
• Investment in public health improves population health and life expectancy-Healthy people
  • are more productive and co ntribute to the economy - Reduces medical expenses for poor
  • households, promoting financial inclusion -Strengthens human capital, supporting skilled
  • workforce development- Promotes equity by providing access to healthcare for all, including
  • marginalized groups- Reduces disease burden, improving school attendance and workforce
  • participation- Example – Kerala’s NRHM and local health initiatives reduced infant mortality
  • to 7 per 1,000 (NFHS -5)-Supports sustainable development goals by improving health,
  • education, and economic growth together.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe and distinguish the benefits of investing in education and the benefits of investing in health, as both are important parts of human capital formation?
questions.solution_html:
• Education improves knowledge, skills, and productivity of individuals -Leads to higher
  • earnings and better job opportunities-Promotes social awareness and participation in civic life-
  • Health investment improves physical and mental well -being- Healthy people are more
  • productive and active in work and learning -Reduces disease burden and medical costs,
  • especially for poor families -Both together strengthen human capital, enhancing economic
  • growth and development - Example – In Kerala, high literacy rate (96%) and good health
  • outcomes support skilled workforce and low infant mortality (7 per 1,000 live births, NFHS -

questions.question: Discuss the role of government policy measures in reducing moral hazard in the health insurance sector.
questions.solution_html:
• Moral hazard occurs when insured people overuse healthcare services-Government policies
  • reduce this risk by regulating health insurance plans- Introduces co-payments, deductibles, and
  • coverage limits to control overuse -Promotes preventive care programs to reduce long-term
  • claims- Monitors insurance companies to ensure fair pricing and claims-Encourages awareness
  • among insured individuals about responsible use of services - Example – India’s Ayushman
  • Bharat PM -JAY includes checks to prevent over -treatment-Reduces un necessary expenses,
  • improves financial sustainability, and ensures better access to essential health services -
  • Supports equity and efficiency in the health sector.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse the role of local governments in public health and sanitation. How effective are they as grassroots implementers, and what limits their potential?
questions.solution_html:
• Local governments in Kerala implement primary healthcare and sanitation programs -
  • Manage PHCs, Sub -Centres, waste di sposal, and water supply -Promote community health
  • awareness and preventive measures -Example – Kerala Panchayats successfully implement
  • clean Kerala campaign and vector control programs- Effective as grassroots implementers due
  • to local knowledge and community participation -Limitations include fund constraints, staff
  • shortages, and coordination issues -Political interference and weak monitoring reduce
  • efficiency-Despite challenges, local governments improve access, reduce disease b urden, and
  • support public health policies in rural areas- Their role is crucial for inclusive and sustainable
  • health development.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
